extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Agriculture in India — Agriculture is the main occupation of the majority of Indians. Types of crops: Kharif (sown in monsoon, harvested in autumn — rice, maize, cotton), Rabi (sown in winter, harvested in spring — wheat, gram, mustard), Cash crops (grown for sale — cotton, sugarcane, jute), Plantation crops (tea, coffee, rubber). India is a major producer of rice, wheat, sugarcane, tea, and cotton. (2) Industries in India — Industries convert raw materials into finished products. Types: Agro-based (uses farm products — textiles, sugar, jute), Mineral-based (uses minerals — steel, cement, aluminum), Heavy industries (large machines, big investment — steel plants, shipbuilding), Small scale (handicrafts, handlooms), IT industry (software, technology services — Bangalore, Hyderabad). Industries provide employment and help the economy grow. (3) Transport in India — Modes: Road (trucks, buses, cars — flexible, good for short distances), Rail (trains — carry heavy goods long distances), Water (ships, boats — cheapest for heavy cargo, ports like Mumbai, Chennai), Air (airplanes — fastest but expensive), Pipeline (for oil and gas transport). Transport connects producers to consumers and helps trade. (4) Population rural and urban — Rural areas: villages, farming as main occupation, simple lifestyle, lower population density. Urban areas: cities, industries and services, modern facilities (malls, hospitals, schools), higher population density. India's population is large and growing. Challenges: providing food, education, healthcare, and jobs for all. Misconceptions: 'most Indians work in IT' (WRONG — agriculture is the main occupation of the majority of Indians; IT employs a smaller but growing percentage), 'all industries are the same' (WRONG — industries are classified by raw materials: agro-based, mineral-based, heavy, small-scale, and IT), 'water transport is the fastest' (WRONG — air transport is the fastest; water transport is the cheapest for heavy cargo but slow), 'rural areas have more people than urban areas' (PARTIALLY TRUE in India — more people live in rural areas, but urban population is growing rapidly due to migration), 'cities are always better than villages' (WRONG — both have advantages and challenges; rural areas provide food, urban areas provide industries and services).
